doc: I work out what the OTHER person changed by comparing the line the person opened with the line as it is now (an empty location reads Office, the table's own word).

symbols.name: rebaseEntry
symbols.sig: export function rebaseEntry(base: FormValues, mine: FormValues, theirs: FormValues): { values: FormValues; kept: Array<keyof FormValues>; overlaps: Array<keyof FormValues> }
symbols.returns: { values: FormValues; kept: Array<keyof FormValues>; overlaps: Array<keyof FormValues> }
doc: I made this THE THREE-WAY MERGE for a line. `base` is the form as it was when the person opened the line, `mine` what is in the form now, `theirs` the line as it is now. A field the person CHANGED keeps his value; every other field takes THEIR value, so he can never put back what the other person changed. `overlaps` are the fields BOTH changed to different values (his is kept, and he is told to look).

symbols.name: HistoryList
symbols.sig: export function HistoryList({ history }: { history: PaxAuditView[] })
doc: The history as a table (my request, 31 Oct 2026): Department, Location, the number, and who did it (name, ticket number, designation). I added two columns that say WHAT was done and WHEN, because without them an added line and a deleted line look the same. For a change I show the new line and say the old one under "Changed"; for a deleted line, the line that went; an authorisation or a withdrawal has no line, so the executive concerned is named under the action and the three line columns show a dash. A coloured dot marks the kind of action.
